mode: Image API through bundled imagegen CLI
workflow: Three quiet base images first, then four independent transparent terrain/camp modules; chapter-one style references only.

files.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one opaque 1024x1536 portrait BASE GROUND TEXTURE for a high-altitude top-down aircraft game. This is only an underlying surface, not a finished map, terrain arrangement or landscape.

Image 1 is the APPROVED CHAPTER ONE painted island. Match the actual painting language of its quiet grassy ground: broad matte color planes, softly visible short painterly brushwork, calm stylized anime game illustration, restrained detail, clean light, gentle cool shadows. Image 2 is the chapter-one ocean base and shows the low-detail role and overall contrast level only. Do NOT copy the water, wave shapes, diagonal current bands, island silhouette, greenery, buildings, or roads from either reference.

Produce BASE A: a quiet old blue-ice floor extending uniformly over the entire canvas. The ice is solid, matte-to-satin and very subtly translucent, in muted slate blue, dusty cyan and soft blue-gray. Suggested value family is #416f87 to #6492a3, with only small tonal differences between broad patches. It must read as a painted game floor, not a close-up photograph of real ice. Match chapter one's soft gouache-like surface treatment and simplified material shading. Let irregular wide blended color patches and sparse soft brush marks suggest age and frost beneath the surface; do not draw recognizable ripples, bands, strips, current flow or concentric shapes. Most of the surface is quiet mid-value blue-gray. No bright highlights or pure white areas.

Keep all four edges at the same general color/value and detail density, suitable for scrolling and repeated terrain modules. No vignette, frame, big dark edge, horizon, perspective convergence, left/right banks or central channel. The light is softly and uniformly overhead, consistent with the reference's upper-left illumination but with no directional cast shadows on this flat surface.

STRICT CONTENT LIMIT: no objects, landmasses, islands, coastlines, snow banks, ice cliffs, ridges, boulders, mountains, jagged slabs, open water, fissures, cracks, veins, white fracture webs, frozen bubbles, snowflakes, speckled frost, sparkling grains, buildings, igloos, tents, paths, roads, tracks, trees, clouds or fog. Those will be added as separate modules in a later step. Do not bake any architecture or raised terrain into this base image.

No photorealistic texture, no crisp microdetail, no procedural noise, no marble texture, no thick outlines, no plastic render, no high contrast. No UI, aircraft, bullets, characters, labels, text, watermark or collage. One finished original portrait painting of ONLY a subdued, softly hand-painted blue-ice base surface, completely edge-to-edge and opaque.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one opaque 1024x1536 portrait BASE GROUND TEXTURE for a high-altitude top-down aircraft game. A reusable flat surface only; not a complete level.

Image 1 is the newly accepted blue-ice base: match its restrained material detail, overall value family and brush scale. Image 2 is the approved FIRST CHAPTER painted island: match its broad matte ground color planes and soft hand-painted game illustration style, especially the quiet grassy surfaces between vegetation. Do not copy its tropical subject, islands, coast, green color, buildings or roads.

Produce BASE B: a FLAT icefield surface covered with a very thin, continuous dusting of snow. The snow lies flush on the ground, with no banks, raised drifts or terrain forms. Use subdued silver blue, cool chalk-blue and very gentle pale ivory-gray brush patches; overall dominant color remains a medium cool blue-gray rather than white. Suggested mid-value family is #809bab to #a6b5bd, with sparse cooler gray-blue passages. Tiny amounts of the underlying darker ice can softly show through, but never as a crack, hole or water opening. Snow looks like a broad matte painted wash with simple, softly broken color planes, not photographic powdered snow. Maintain chapter one's clean painterly simplification and calm low contrast.

The entire canvas is the same low-relief material, seen straight down, with consistent upper-left soft daylight but no object cast shadows. Keep all four edges similar in color/value for scrolling. Low-frequency, irregular gentle brush marks are welcome; no obvious directional stripes, repeated bands, wave shapes, tiled geometry, large central accent or vignette. Preserve large quiet areas for aircraft and projectiles.

STRICT CONTENT LIMIT: no landscape composition, raised terrain, banks, cliffs, ridges, boulders, mountains, shorelines, islands, ice slabs, crystals, cracks, veins, white fracture webs, open water, bubbles, sparkle, flakes or granular speckling. No buildings, igloos, tents, roads, tracks, vegetation, props, clouds or fog; those come later as separate modules. This must remain a neutral underlying ground image.

No pure-white glare, high-frequency texture, detailed realistic frost, marble veining, procedural noise, heavy outlines or 3D plastic. No text, labels, logos, UI, aircraft, bullets, characters or collage. One original finished portrait base texture, edge-to-edge and opaque.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one opaque 1024x1536 portrait BASE GROUND TEXTURE for a high-altitude top-down aircraft game. Only the flat underlying material; buildings and raised terrain are separate later assets.

Image 1 is the accepted blue-ice base. Preserve its cold muted palette, soft broad brush scale, low-contrast painted material and simple game-background finish. Image 2 is the approved FIRST CHAPTER painted island, a style reference for clean gently brushed matte surfaces; no tropical subject or objects should be copied.

Produce BASE C: a quiet flat TRANSITION surface between old blue ice and a thin dusting of snow. Mid-value desaturated slate-cyan ice remains visible through broad, irregular, feathered pale blue-gray snow washes. The snow coverage is light and patchy, with blended amorphous shapes, not detached snowbanks or raised lumps. Approximately half the surface has slightly lighter cool brush patches, with the other half a calm medium blue-gray. Keep colors between the blue-ice base and a thin-snow base: roughly #65889c to #99aeb9. No strong white shapes, dark holes, hard borders, cracks or contrasty lines.

Match chapter one's hand-painted environmental language: gently interlocking broad color planes, a few understated short gouache-like brush marks, soft clean daylight and restrained form. This is a neutral overhead surface swatch, not an illustration of a valley, a river, a shoreline, an ice sheet seen from the side or an isometric diorama. Do not create long diagonal wave bands, swirling paths, a bright center, repeated rows or regular patterns. Keep the four edges close in average value and material density so the base can scroll and blend with neighboring sections.

STRICT CONTENT LIMIT: no buildings, igloos, tents, camps, equipment, footsteps, roads, vegetation, stones, raised drifts, ice walls, shelves, glaciers, snowbanks, fissures, ice cracks, crystal spikes, open water, splashing, frozen bubbles, speckled frost, glitter, dense grains, clouds, fog, UI or weather particles. No separate objects at all. Keep all future landforms and architecture out of this base layer.

No photographic microdetail, sharp white vein network, marble texture, procedural noise, strong outlines, plastic 3D shading, text, logos, aircraft, characters or contact sheet. One finished original opaque portrait base surface, filling every edge.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one original reusable RGBA TERRAIN MODULE on a genuinely transparent background, square 1024x1024. This is one small modular scenery region, NOT a whole map or a scene with a horizon.

Image 1 is the approved FIRST CHAPTER painted island. Closely match its gently brushed anime-background art, broad matte color planes, readable organic shapes, restrained detail and near-overhead aerial camera. Image 2 is the new blue-ice base underneath this module and is the palette/edge-compositing reference. Change the subject to a polar terrain patch; do not copy the island outline, tropical vegetation, roads, sea or facilities.

Paint one low, gently undulating snow-covered ground patch, irregular and asymmetrical in outline, occupying about 75 percent of the square canvas. Soft silver-blue shaded snow and muted ivory upper surfaces, with a few shallow satin blue-ice exposures. A small group of two or three low gray rocks sits near one edge. Most of the patch is calm open snow with broad simple brush planes and minimal marks. Keep the relief VERY LOW, like a modest snow berm seen from high altitude, not a tall ice island, sheer cliff or floating rock. No dark vertical rim, no thick rock cross-section around the perimeter. Near-top-down camera, roofs/upper surfaces dominant, no horizon or frontal side view.

The irregular outer edge should feather through thin powder snow into real transparent alpha, so it blends over the muted blue-ice base. No rectangular or oval backing plate, no black/white/colored matte, no checkerboard. The full patch is visible with a small transparent margin on all sides. It must feel grounded when composited, with only soft upper-left daylight shading and subtle contact darkening at rocks.

No buildings, igloos, tents, trees, roads, paths, footprints, vehicles, crystal spikes, open water, dramatic fissures, dense ice cracks, white webbing, photographic snow grains, glitter, heavy noise, plastic 3D highlights, comic outlines, fog, clouds, particles, labels, UI or text. One clean original transparent snow-terrain module with the same simplified painted finish as chapter one.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one original reusable RGBA low ICE RIDGE terrain module, genuinely transparent background, 1024x1024 square. One modular feature, not a full map.

Image 1 is the project's approved FIRST CHAPTER painted island: match its near-overhead aerial camera, broad readable hand-painted color planes, softly brushed matte finish, gentle upper-left light and clean anime-game simplicity. Image 2 is the underlying muted blue-ice floor, a color and compositing reference. No tropical subject, water, greenery, roads or buildings from the reference should appear.

Create an asymmetric low pressure ridge of blue ice, consisting of a few broad gently fractured plates and rounded snow-covered shoulders. Think of a shallow seam where frozen ice plates have pushed together, seen from high altitude. Pale dusty cyan lit planes, cool slate-blue shallow sides, soft ivory snow settled on top. Keep this a low broad feature, not a towering glacier, crystalline spike, jagged ice wall, upright boulder pile or isometric display object. Only a little shallow side relief should be visible. The main shape is loosely curved or kinked and irregular, with quiet flat snow beside it. Simplify into a handful of coherent planes; no hairline fracture network or realistic micro-ice texture.

The feature occupies roughly 70–80 percent of the canvas and is fully visible. Outer thin snow/ice edges dissolve softly into genuine alpha, suitable for layering on the supplied base ground. No square/oval backing, hard cutout outline, detached floating platform, thick dark perimeter, black/white matte or checkerboard. All shading belongs to the ridge itself; no huge cast shadow or surrounding painted map.

No water river, canyon, coast, houses, people, equipment, trees, roads, paths, tiny debris field, glitter, particles, clouds, labels, UI, aircraft or text. The final asset is one quiet high-altitude hand-painted ice-pressure-ridge module matching the actual chapter-one scenery style.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one original reusable RGBA POLAR IGLOO CAMP scenery module on a genuinely transparent background, 1024x1024 square. The camp and its snow footing are one integrated painted region, like a facility integrated into the chapter-one island.

Image 1 is the approved FIRST CHAPTER island. Copy its gentle matte hand-painted anime-environment language, broad simple surface planes, soft clean daylight, near-overhead aerial camera and small building scale. Image 2 is the muted blue-ice floor this module will sit on; use it for cold color relationships and softly blending perimeter. Do not copy tropical greenery, sea, island cliffs, concrete roads or harbor buildings.

Create a small camp of three modest snow-block dome igloos grounded in one broad low irregular patch of snow. The snow ground covers most of the module, with the three tiny igloos clustered towards one side and generous quiet snow around them. Each igloo is only about 5–7 percent of the whole canvas width, emphasizing high flight altitude. Show softly rounded snow-block roofs, very short low tunnel entrances, subtle blue contact shadows and a tiny restrained warm orange doorway. Add one miniature wooden sled and a few close-packed supply bundles; a handful of faint short footsteps connects only nearby entrances. No people or caricatures. Roofs dominate the view, only a sliver of low side surface is visible. No large front-facing houses, oversized dome, icon-style thick outlines or toy-like bevels.

Integrate every object into the same snow patch with partly buried bases and coherent soft upper-left shadows, as in the reference's facilities attached to their island ground. Snow uses soft ivory and silver blue; a little muted cyan ice shows through near the perimeter. Low gray rocks may anchor one edge, kept sparse. Broad hand-painted shading, calm open areas and restrained tiny details. Avoid photographic ice, noisy frost, crack webs and harsh specular dots.

The entire ground patch is visible, occupying about 80 percent of a square canvas. Its asymmetrical powder-snow perimeter feathers gently into true alpha, without a raised island rim or cliff. No square/oval backing plate, black/white matte, checkerboard, surrounding full scene, river, mountains, crystal spires, trees, fog, clouds, particles, UI, aircraft, labels or text. Final image: one clean transparent modular camp region in the same actual visual style as chapter one.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one original reusable RGBA POLAR RESEARCH CAMP module, genuine transparent background, 1024x1024 square. A complete small scenery region with its own grounded snow footing, not a whole level.

Image 1 is the approved FIRST CHAPTER painted island. Match its softly brushed matte anime-game painting, simplified broad shapes, clean upper-left illumination, near-overhead aerial camera and tiny grounded facilities. Image 2 is the muted blue-ice base, a palette and edge-compositing reference. Replace tropical scenery entirely with a modest polar camp; do not copy grass, sea, island cliffs or asphalt roads.

On one low irregular snow patch, place two tiny squat blue-gray prefab research cabins, one with a small roof radar dish and a short antenna. Two very small low muted-orange expedition tents and a miniature supply sled sit nearby on the same snow ground. Each cabin should be only about 6–8 percent of the full canvas width, each tent about 3–4 percent; the whole group occupies only one quarter of the region, with broad calm snow filling the rest. Add a few tiny close-packed supplies and faint short foot tracks connecting the group. A few warm window accents are enough. No helipad, large symbols, oversized radar, tall tower, large concrete platform, people or vehicles.

Use a high aerial almost-top-down view, with top surfaces dominant and only a thin shallow side face visible. Objects are partly banked in snow and have small coherent contact shadows, painted together with their footing. Low soft snow drifts, one or two exposed gray rocks, subtle dusty cyan ice near an edge. Clean ivory/cool-blue planes with gentle gouache-like brushwork, not photorealistic grains, thick outlines, hard toy renders, crack networks or dirty textures.

The full asymmetrical ground patch is visible with transparent margins and softly feathered powder-snow edges that blend onto the supplied base. No rectangular or oval backing plate, no thick island cliff rim, floating rock underside, black/white/colored matte or checkerboard. No full landscape, coast, river, tree line, crystal spires, fog, clouds, particles, aircraft, text, UI, labels or watermark. One original transparent modular research-camp region matching chapter one's grounded painted facilities.
